title: Vietnamese Rice Paper Breakfast Flatbread with Crispy Pork and Eggs
summary: Start your morning with a popular street-food favourite adapted into a crisp, savory Vietnamese flatbread. Built upon a base of thin rice paper toasted over low heat, this morning dish is brushed with beaten egg, scallion oil, and spicy chili paste to create a golden, flavorful crust. Savory minced pork, dried shrimp flakes, and fried shallots are layered across the top, delivering an incredible balance of crunchy textures and deeply satisfying umami note. A light drizzle of creamy mayo and tangy sriracha completes the assembly before folding or slicing into shareable portions. Perfectly tailored for a quick breakfast routine, this recipe transforms simple pantry staples into a vibrant pan-roasted flatbread filled with aromatic flair. Enjoy it hot right out of the skillet alongside fresh herbs for a unique morning culinary experience that offers both balanced protein and quick preparation.

steps.step: Slice four green scallion stalks thinly into tiny round rings using a sharp chef knife.
Heat two tablespoons vegetable oil in a small pan until shimmering hot over medium heat.
Pour hot oil over chopped scallions in a small heatproof bowl to make scallion oil.
Mince one garlic clove finely and set aside on cutting board for cooking ground pork.
Heat butter in skillet over medium-high heat until bubbly and completely melted.
Add minced pork and garlic to skillet, crumbling meat into small bits with spatula.
Season pork with fish sauce, soy sauce, sugar, and black pepper, stirring frequently.
Sauté ground pork for six minutes until fully cooked through and crispy around edges.
Transfer crisp pork to a small bowl and set aside near your flatbread cooking station.
Finely chop dried shrimp using a sharp knife until reduced to small savory specks.
Whisk eggs, water, and pinch of salt together in a shallow dish until smooth yellow mixture.
Slice fresh jalapeno thinly into round rings for garnishing flatbread at assembly time.
Unwrap cheese slices and cut into small soft pieces ready to spread on warm flatbread.
Clean skillet thoroughly with paper towel before starting the rice paper base roasting.
Place one dry sheet of rice paper flat inside dry nonstick skillet over low flame.
Brush top surface of rice paper with one tablespoon prepared scallion oil right away.
Pour two tablespoons beaten egg mixture directly onto center of warming rice paper sheet.
Use back of spoon to spread egg evenly across surface, staying near edges carefully.
Dot soft cheese pieces over egg layer so they begin melting from skillet heat below.
Sprinkle seasoned ground pork evenly across top of setting egg layer in skillet base.
Scatter chopped dried shrimp flakes over meat to add deep savory seafood flavor notes.
Drizzle chili oil and hoisin sauce evenly across surface using quick zig-zag motions.
Cook flatbread for three minutes on low until bottom of rice paper turns crisp and golden.
Check bottom edges using spatulas to ensure base does not burn while egg sets completely.
Sprinkle crispy fried shallots evenly across warm melted cheese and cooked egg layer.
Drizzle mayonnaise and sriracha sauce in crosshatch pattern over cooked flatbread top.
Fold flatbread in half like taco or keep flat, cooking ten additional seconds to set.
Slide golden cooked flatbread carefully onto clean wooden cutting board for final slicing.
Repeat cooking process for remaining rice paper sheets and toppings to yield four portions.
Slice each folded flatbread into three triangular handheld pieces using kitchen shears.
Scatter fresh cilantro leaves across sliced flatbread portions on board for brightness.
Garnish slices with jalapeno rounds to add optional fresh fiery spice to each bite.
Sprinkle toasted sesame seeds evenly over decorated flatbread pieces before serving hot.
Drizzle sesame oil lightly over fresh cilantro garnish to enhance warm nutty aroma.
Arrange sliced flatbread pieces neatly on warm serving platter alongside lime wedges.
Serve immediately while rice paper crust remains ultra crisp and cheese stays melted.
Provide extra sriracha and mayonnaise dipping dishes on table for added customization.
Ensure flatbread bottoms remain dry by serving on wooden board or parchment paper.
Instruct guests to squeeze fresh lime juice over warm toppings just before eating.
Pair breakfast flatbread with hot Vietnamese iced coffee for full traditional style.
Check crispiness of flatbread edge before serving to confirm ideal texture match.
Enjoy immediately as vibrant breakfast item rich in crisp textures and bold spices.
